transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-05
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Omar Salazar (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Verdant), Tom Greer (Verdant), Nina Wood (Verdant)
Shared artifacts: Redwood hosted embeddings quickstart notebook (link), pilot pricing spreadsheet (one pager), security pack (SOC2 + KMS notes)

[00:00] Lena (Redwood): Hi everyone, thanks for carving time. I'm Lena from Redwood, AE on the account, and with me is Omar our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Priya (Verdant): Hey Lena, good thanks. Excited to see how you handle embeddings + reranking — our search relevance has been a bit patchy.
[00:18] Lena: Great — quick agenda: we'll do a short qual to confirm constraints, then Omar will show the hosted API flow — embeddings then reranker — demo the console for Optimize suggestions, and we'll finish with next steps. Sound ok?
[00:30] Tom (Verdant): Sounds good. We're short on time but this is the right agenda.

Qualification and context (00:40 - 08:00)
[00:40] Lena: Priya, can you quickly summarize your stack and what 'patchy' looks like — e.g., recall vs precision, latency targets, SLA?
[00:50] Priya: Sure. We run a hybrid retrieval pipeline — OpenSearch for initial retrieval, then a light BERT re-ranker for the top 100. Freshness is important — content updates multiple times a day. Our p99 latency target is ~300ms for end-to-end in-app search, and we're doing around 3–10M queries/month depending on the spike. Cost has become a concern; our infra team is looking at offloading inference.
[01:20] Lena: Helpful. Are you open to hosted inference or do you require private/VPC from the start?
[01:25] Priya: Initially hosted is fine for a pilot; we'll need VPC/on-prem conversation later for regulated subsets. SOC2 is a must.
[01:35] Omar (Redwood): Noted — hosted pilot plus a path to private/Dedicated later is common. We can show how routing and fallbacks work. Quick question, how are you storing vectors today?
[01:45] Nina (Verdant): Right now vectors live in an OpenSearch plugin — it's been okay but scaling vector ops is gnarly.
[01:53] Omar: Ok. Two common approaches: keep vectors in a vector DB and call Redwood embeddings for ingestion, or precompute vectors and store them where you like. Both supported; hosted embeddings endpoint can also be used in a batch ingest flow.

Demo + Walkthrough (08:00 - 30:00)
[08:00] Omar: I'm going to share my screen — showing the Redwood Console. First, embeddings endpoint — we send a POST with the text, get back a 1536-d vector (demo model). Note: model choice and dimensionality depends on the model you pick.
[08:20] [screen share] Omar: Here is a quick curl example, and the console shows token-level cost and latency. We have a live example — I pasted three docs, we call /embeddings, vectors come back.
[08:38] Tom: Quick Q — can we control batch sizes and concurrency? Our ingestion process is huge.
[08:44] Omar: Yes. The hosted API supports multi-document batching; the Optimize tab will suggest batch sizes and caching settings based on your traffic shape. We also have a recommended autopilot for batching that trades latency for throughput.
[09:05] Priya: How do you recommend we build the index — store raw vectors in OpenSearch or use a managed vector db?
[09:12] Omar: If you already have a vector-enabled OpenSearch cluster and it meets your latency and cardinality needs, it's fine. For scale, many customers move to a dedicated vector DB for sharding/faster ANN. Redwood is DB-agnostic. We also show per-route latency and token cost so you can iterate.
[09:34] [15:00] Omar: Now the reranker endpoint — this is a hosted endpoint that accepts retrieval candidates and returns scores + optional rewritten answers. The typical pattern: retrieve top-K (e.g., 100) using ANN, then call reranker to re-score top 10 and produce a final sort. This reduces cost versus re-ranking all hits with a heavy model.
[15:28] Nina: Does reranker run on the same model family as embeddings? Latency tradeoffs?
[15:33] Omar: Rerankers are often smaller encoder-decoder or cross-encoders optimized for precision. We surface model profiled p50/p95/p99 latencies in the console. You can pick a cheaper reranker or a heavier one and do blended scoring — e.g., 0.6 * BM25 + 0.4 * reranker score. We demo scoring mixes in the console.
[16:05] [18:00] Omar: Here's an example payload: you provide query, candidate snippets, and options like top_k and score_mix. Response includes normalized scores and debug tokens for explainability.

Latency, cost, reliability conversation (18:30 - 27:00)
[18:30] Tom: For our p99 300ms, what does that map to if we use hosted?
[18:38] Omar: Depends on model size and concurrency. For a mid-sized reranker model we typically see 60–120ms per call p95 on dedicated. Hosted has slightly higher variance depending on routing, but with our autoscaling and prefork pools most pilots hit under 200ms p95 for reranker-only calls. For end-to-end you need to budget retrieval + rerank + network. We'll run a projection for your 10M q/mo.
[19:10] Priya: And cost? We're sensitive.
[19:15] Lena: We'll include per-token and per-embedding pricing in the pilot doc. Our Optimize tab suggests quantization and batching to reduce unit cost; for example, INT8 quantization for certain model variants reduces cost 2–3x with minimal quality loss for reranking workloads.
[19:40] Nina: Any gotchas for caching? We have lots of repeated queries.
[19:45] Omar: Prefix and KV caching can help for chat-like flows; in search, caching top-K candidates is common. Redwood's runtime has automatic prefix caching and you can configure TTLs in the console. Note: transcription might show KV as "K V cash" in some exports :)

Security / Compliance (27:00 - 32:00)
[27:00] Priya: SOC2 is required; do you provide detailed logs and KMS integration?
[27:10] Lena: Yes. We provide SOC2 artifacts in the security pack, we support customer-managed KMS for private/Dedicated, and audit logs are surfaced in the Console. For hosted we have encryption at rest and in transit, and options to redact PII during ingestion.
[27:40] Tom: SSO and RBAC — our security team will want SAML.
[27:45] Lena: SAML SSO, SCIM, and fine-grained RBAC are supported for account access. We'll attach the SAML playbook in the follow-up email.

Quick Optimize demo (32:00 - 36:00)
[32:00] Omar: Switching to Optimize — it analyzes token distribution and suggests batch sizes, caching TTLs, and quantization candidates. For your workload shape it's recommending smaller batch sizes at low concurrency to hit 300ms p99 but suggests INT8 for the reranker to lower cost.
[32:35] Nina: Can we run A/B tests from the Console?
[32:40] Omar: Yes — the rollout module supports canary/A-B with automatic fallback policy. You can route a percent to a new model and compare metrics. We also store evals attached to prompt sets so regressions are caught.

POC and pilot planning (36:00 - 40:00)
[36:00] Lena: For next steps we typically propose a 4–6 week hosted pilot: week 1 ingest + baseline evals, week 2 tune reranker mix, week 3 run perf benchmarks, week 4 compare quality & decide on scale/Dedicated path. Does that timeline fit?
[36:20] Priya: Yes, that sounds practical. We'll need the security questionnaire answered in parallel.
[36:28] Lena: We'll send the security pack and the pilot pricing spreadsheet after this call.

Recap + Close (40:00 - 42:00)
[40:00] Lena: Quick recap: we showed hosted embeddings endpoint and reranker flow, console Optimize suggestions, and discussed pilot plan and security requirements. Action items: Lena sends pricing + security pack; Omar runs the latency/cost projection; Verdant shares sample dataset and SSO requirements.
[40:30] Tom: Great. Looking forward to the benchmark.
[40:35] Priya: Thanks everyone. We'll try to get the data to you early next week.
[40:45] Lena: Thanks, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the POC kickoff.
[40:52] Omar: Bye all.
[40:55] Meeting ended.
